Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

common adjective

found or happening often; ordinary

also commonly, very common, widespread, commonplace

classical

Phaedr. 3.9.1: vulgāre amīcī nōmen
Cic. de Or. 1.248: in commūnī vītā et vulgārī hominum cōnsuētūdine (Lewis & Short)

vulgāris, vulgāre

common, ordinary, met with everywhere

Of the many, so also commonplace; the adverb is vulgō, commonly (see popular).

Examples

  • vulgāre amīcī nōmen, sed rāra est fidēs

    the name of friend is common, but loyalty is rarePhaedr. 3.9.1

  • quibus nōn vulgāris in cursū gradus, sed mollis alternō crūrum explicātū glomerātiō

    whose pace in running is not the common one, but a soft rolling gait, the legs thrown out by turnsPlin. NH 8.166

Other words

  • pervulgātus, pervulgāta, pervulgātum — very common, commonplace

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 5.16.2: cōnsōlātiō pervulgāta quidem illa maximē

See also normal, popular, general, average.

SourcesLewis & Short: vulgaris · Lewis & Short: pervulgo

Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
